name: Nicotine

lead: Nicotine is the main psychoactive alkaloid in tobacco. It is sold in cigarettes, vapes, oral pouches, gum, lozenges and patches. Regulated nicotine replacement products are marketed to reduce withdrawal and craving in people quitting smoking.

In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a way to suppress appetite and 'leanmaxx', and as a focus aid. Other posters describe it as harmful to looks, citing sleep, skin, teeth, hair and anxiety complaints. The cessation literature is large; the evidence for any appearance or fat-loss use specifically is thin.

paras: Nicotine activates nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, prompting release of dopamine and other neurotransmitters. Forum posts attribute appetite suppression and higher energy expenditure to this action; those posts cite older physiological studies that are not evaluated in this article's sources.

Nicotine is addictive, raises heart rate and blood pressure, and the FDA-listed labels for nicotine gum caution people with heart disease and pregnant users. E-cigarettes and pouches have been studied for oral and other effects, with long-term data still accumulating. Forum users report insomnia, anxiety, palpitations and dependence.

lead: Nicotine is a plant alkaloid found chiefly in the tobacco plant and is the principal addictive component of tobacco products. It acts on nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in the nervous system and increases release of dopamine and other neurotransmitters [1][2]. It was isolated in 1828 according to one encyclopedic summary [3].

Regulated nicotine products such as gum, lozenges and patches are used in nicotine replacement therapy to ease withdrawal during smoking cessation [4][5][6]. The US label for nicotine polacrilex gum states that it reduces withdrawal symptoms, including craving, associated with quitting smoking, and warns that nicotine can raise heart rate and blood pressure [7].

In looksmaxxing communities, nicotine is discussed mainly as an appetite suppressant and stimulant for cutting body fat, with newer threads centred on oral pouches. Other community members argue that it harms appearance, and some report quitting as improving it. No clinical study found for this article has tested nicotine as an appearance or fat-loss intervention.

Over-the-counter as replacement products in many countries; tobacco regulated

paras: Nicotine replacement therapy delivers nicotine in gum, patches, nasal spray, inhalers and lozenges to reduce the urge to smoke and withdrawal symptoms [5]. A 1990 randomized trial of a transdermal patch in highly dependent smokers found higher abstinence than placebo, along with reduced withdrawal symptoms such as negative affect [6]. Cochrane reviews have assessed NRT and electronic cigarettes as smoking-cessation aids [8][5].
Nicotine has also been studied in other research settings, for example attention and cognition in people with schizophrenia, and a small pilot in sarcoidosis [9][10].

Forum users describe nicotine, particularly pouches and gum, as an appetite suppressant and a way to stay lean during a diet [11][12][13]. One widely read looksmax.org thread presents nicotine as a stimulant for fat loss and lists older physiological studies in support [11]. No randomized trial identified for this article tests nicotine for fat loss, facial leanness or other appearance outcomes.

Nicotine binds nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, ligand-gated ion channels found throughout the central and peripheral nervous system [2]. In rat experiments, nicotine and other drugs that humans misuse increased extracellular dopamine in the nucleus accumbens, a finding frequently cited in discussions of reward and dependence [1].

Studies have compared the pharmacokinetics of nicotine patches and the nicotine delivered by vaping pods [14][15]. Oral nicotine pouches have been the subject of a recent public health review describing their rising popularity [16].

Human trials of nicotine concern smoking cessation, product pharmacokinetics, cognition and physiology rather than appearance. A Cochrane review examines nicotine replacement for long-term cessation [5], and another Cochrane living review examines e-cigarettes for cessation [8]. Randomized trials have also tested patches, nasal spray and lozenges for bioequivalence, attention and oral mucosal effects [17][18][19].

A 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis found that, compared with cigarette smokers, e-cigarette users had a lower chance of bleeding on probing and less plaque, probing depth and attachment loss, while the authors noted comparisons with non-smokers as well [20]. This concerns periodontal health, not appearance directly.

A 2023 meta-analysis of social media use and health risk behaviours in adolescents included tobacco and nicotine vaping among the outcomes; it did not study nicotine's effect on looks [21]. No study found tests whether nicotine reduces body fat in people without a dependence indication, alters facial appearance, hair, collagen or testosterone.

The US label for nicotine polacrilex gum advises people with heart disease, recent heart attack, irregular heartbeat or uncontrolled high blood pressure to ask a doctor before use because nicotine can raise heart rate and blood pressure. It advises pregnant or breast-feeding people to use it only on a health care provider's advice [7].
Nicotine is described across pharmacological literature as dependence-forming, and instruments such as the Fagerström Test have been developed to measure nicotine dependence [22].

Forum users report their own experiences. One poster on looksmax.org attributed insomnia, palpitations, brain fog, hair loss and other symptoms to pouches [23]; other threads discuss anxiety, facial bloating and balding [24][25][26]. These are individual reports and have not been verified in controlled studies. Other users describe feeling better after quitting [27].

Threads such as 'Nicotine for fatloss guide' and 'nicotine for appetite suppression' present nicotine as a tool for leanness and focus, often citing physiological studies on energy expenditure and appetite [11][12]. Some posters argue that pouches are preferable to smoking or vaping because of smell and other considerations [11].

Others dispute this. A thread titled 'Nicotine pouches will destroy you' lists symptoms the author attributes to heavy use [23], and other threads ask whether pouches affect looks [28]. Posts on T Nation mention nicotine in passing, including one user's belief that tobacco use affected gynecomastia, which is the poster's own speculation [29].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org nicotine appears both as a leanmaxxing stimulant and as a feared 'looksmin' factor, with pouches now the most discussed form [11][23][28].

A randomized double-blind trial finds higher abstinence with a transdermal nicotine patch than placebo [6].
Cochrane review of nicotine replacement therapy for smoking cessation published [5].
Cochrane network meta-analysis of electronic cigarettes for smoking cessation updated [8].
